analysis.headline: A richer 1SEO plumbing-and-HVAC build with proper Plumber and HVACBusiness schema and CallRail-instrumented Google Ads, undercut by 17 orphaned pages the internal links never reach.
bluf: A richer 1SEO plumbing-and-HVAC build with proper Plumber and HVACBusiness schema and CallRail-instrumented Google Ads, undercut by 17 orphaned pages the internal links never reach.

Henley's Plumbing & Air sits in Scorpion's book through 1SEO Digital Agency (now Scorpion). Scorpion acquired 1SEO Digital Agency on 2026-06-18; 1SEO's home-services, legal, health and franchise clients moved onto Scorpion's RevenueMAX platform. WordPress with Elementor; CallRail call tracking and a Google Ads tag are wired through GTM. Richer schema than the Coalmarch book, but internal linking leaves many sitemap URLs orphaned.
The on-page read returned 5 findings (0 High, 3 Medium) and 1 compliance observations; the overall grade is C.
The deepest schema in the Scorpion book (Plumber, HVACBusiness, Article, Person, FAQ), a posted license number, correct index/follow directives, and server-rendered content.

win_watch_next.win: The deepest schema in the Scorpion book (Plumber, HVACBusiness, Article, Person, FAQ), a posted license number, correct index/follow directives, and server-rendered content.
win_watch_next.watch: Google Ads and GA4 fire through GTM on load; the license number is correctly posted, so the exposure is the pre-consent tag firing, not a disclosure gap.
win_watch_next.next: Henley's is the one site in the book visibly running Google Ads (tag AW-17032377429) with CallRail (205364564) attribution, so a landing-page and conversion-tracking read on the live campaign is the highest-value paid move.

key_judgments.title: The defects are the agency's template, not the owner's choices
key_judgments.judgment: It is likely that the recurring defects on Henley's Plumbing & Air are inherited from the 1SEO Digital Agency (now Scorpion) template and platform rather than owned by the business, because The Elementor build, the GTM-mediated CallRail and Google Ads wiring and the orphaned-location-page pattern are template-level; the license numbers and NAP that are correct are owned by the business.
falsifiers: A sibling site on the same template without the same defect would weaken this.
An owner-made change that post-dates the agency build would reassign ownership.

key_judgments.title: The site wins its own name but loses the money searches
key_judgments.judgment: It is very likely that the site captures brand demand but not non-brand demand, because the brand appears in Autocomplete only for its own name while the city+service money terms surface rivals.
falsifiers: A GSC export showing non-brand impressions/clicks at volume would overturn this.
A map-pack screenshot ranking the client for the money terms would overturn this.

key_judgments.title: A challenger can lead with a clean ownership-and-diagnosis contrast
key_judgments.judgment: It is likely that a challenger who leads with a declared audit plus true site ownership can open a conversation, because the lock-in and the inherited defects are public and documented.
falsifiers: A long contract term with heavy exit penalties would lengthen the cycle.
High owner satisfaction despite the defects would weaken the wedge.

findings.title: 17 pages are orphan candidates
findings.evidence: 17 sitemap URLs had no internal in-link among the crawled pages (e.g. https://www.henleysplumbingair.com/11-of-the-most-common-causes-of-a-leaky-pipe/); link equity does not reach them and Google may treat them as low-value.
findings.fix: Add internal links from hubs and related service/location pages so every money page is reachable in 2-3 clicks.

findings.title: 20 title tags exceed the snippet limit
findings.evidence: 20 crawled pages carry titles over 70 characters, so Google truncates them in results and the city/service keyword can fall off the visible end.
findings.fix: Rewrite titles to ~55-60 characters, front-loading the service and city.

findings.title: LocalBusiness schema omits recommended fields
findings.evidence: The LocalBusiness/▸ markup is missing recommended fields (image, geo, openingHoursSpecification, priceRange, sameAs, areaServed across the audited pages); each raises eligibility for local rich results.
findings.fix: Complete the LocalBusiness block with geo, hours, priceRange, image and sameAs links to the GBP and socials.

findings.title: A countdown timer resets on every reload (fake urgency)
findings.evidence: The page shows a countdown that resets to the same value on reload (['40:14', '00:00', '32:46', '00:00', '00:00']), a fabricated-urgency pattern the FTC has named in enforcement.
findings.fix: Remove the resetting timer or make it reflect a real, fixed deadline.

findings.title: Invisible on the money searches; present only on its own name
findings.evidence: In Google Autocomplete the brand appears for 0 of 0 seeds (its own name and close variants) but is absent from the non-brand money terms: . Answer engines and the map pack reward entities that own the non-brand term; this site owns only its brand.
findings.fix: Win the non-brand terms with complete local entity data, city+service pages and citations; name an AI-crawler posture in robots.txt.

exposure.rule: FTC guidance on fake urgency/countdown timers
exposure.cite: FTC, Bringing Dark Patterns to Light (2022)
exposure.base_rate: FTC has acted on fabricated urgency, but rarely against a single SMB service page.
exposure.open_question: Is the timer tied to a genuine promotion deadline, or is it purely cosmetic? One screenshot of the reset settles it.
exposure.channel: Flag to the client; cosmetic timers are easy to remove.

glossary.def: A finding is inherited when it comes from the agency's shared template or platform, owned when the business controls it. It decides who fixes it and who to lead the pitch against.
Ad/analytics tags that run before any consent choice. A privacy exposure under US state laws and GDPR; cheap to fix with a consent banner.
Using schema.org/Product for a service. It has no rich-result path for services and can misdescribe the business to answer engines.
Scorpion's hosting platform. A client site resolving into the scorpcloud CNAME zone is on Scorpion's proprietary CMS - the central lock-in.
A fetch-only run with no client exports. Rankings, traffic and spend are protocols or inferred, not measured.
The intelligence-community probability scale (almost no chance ... almost certain) used so a likelihood word always maps to a number range.
